name: Teo Vasquez-Lind
equipment: Steel-frame fixed-gear bike with no brakes and a front light that still works
Heavy U-lock, carried in a back holster like a sidearm
Leather jacket, patched at both elbows with gaffer tape
Courier bag containing the undelivered package: two padded hard drives addressed to 'Dr. Y. Haddad, Bioacoustics, Merriwick Museum of Natural History — URGENT, HAND DELIVER'
Phone with a cracked screen and 61% battery, and a dying power bank
Two energy bars, a bike pump, a tyre lever and a chain tool
Paper manifest of the day's drops, eleven signatures and one blank line
features: Human (Specialist) (+2 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom, one extra skill proficiency: Streetwise)

Overwatch (reaction: when an enemy you can see moves within your weapon's normal range, make one ranged attack against it; once per short rest — for Teo, that is a thrown box cutter or whatever is to hand)
Trailwise (advantage on Survival checks to track and navigate; the party cannot be surprised while Teo is on watch and conscious)
Weapon proficiencies: Melee, Sidearms, Longarms, Energy Weapons
Local Celebrity (Athlete feature: Teo won the Alleycat Night Race three years running and every courier, deli man and doorman in the Meridian knows his face and will do him a small favour)

personality.traits: I think in routes. Every block in this city is a set of lines to me, and I can tell you which ones are open before you have finished asking. I talk fast, laugh at the wrong moments, and I cannot stand still unless I am hiding.
personality.ideals: Every drop gets delivered. A signature on the line is a promise kept, and I have never once left a line blank.
personality.bonds: The package in my bag, for a man I have never met, marked URGENT in a hand that was shaking when it wrote it. And my mother in Eastgate, who will be worried, who is always worried, who was right.
personality.flaws: Speed is how I solve everything, and running is the single most dangerous thing a person can do on this island now. I am going to have to learn to walk, and I am bad at it.

appearance: A lean, wiry man of twenty-four with a shaved head under a cycling cap worn backwards, a gold stud in one ear and calves like rope. Half-Dominican, half-Swedish, with his mother's colouring and his father's pale eyes. He wears a battered leather jacket over a reflective vest, cut-off cargo shorts in October, and the permanent squint of someone who reads traffic for a living. When he stops moving it looks deliberate, like a held breath.
backstory: Teo Vasquez-Lind has been a bike messenger in the Meridian since he was seventeen, which makes him a veteran in a trade where people last about four years. He knows the island the way rivers know a valley: which lights are long, which doormen let you through the lobby to the back street, which loading docks connect, which of the Lower Ward's alleys go through and which only pretend to. On the Thursday he has one drop left — a pickup from the Harbor Acoustic Monitoring station at Pier Point, two padded drives for a scientist at the Natural History Museum, marked URGENT by a technician who looked, Teo thought, like she had not slept. He is coming up Kestrel Avenue past Union Terminal at 4:12 when every traffic light on the avenue goes to the same colour at once — a colour that is not any of the three — and a hundred and forty cars stop in the same instant without a single horn. He puts a foot down. It is the first time in seven years he has stopped on Kestrel Avenue for anything, and it saves his life, because the man on the bike beside him does not.
